title: 한국 사람 이름 읽기: 성과 이름
objective: By the end, you can split a Korean full name into its surname (성) and given name (이름). You can also say the common surnames 김, 이, 박 and 최 with their Korean sounds, not their English spellings.
summary: In a Korean name, the surname comes first and is usually one syllable. The given name comes after it and is usually two syllables.

task.title: Read Korean names
task.line: Read each name or short dialogue, then write or choose the answer.

words.meaning: polite title, like Mr./Ms. (use it after a given name or full name, not after the surname alone)

letters.as: Like 'geem'; ㄱ is softer than English k. Often spelled Kim.
Like 'ee' in 'see', with no l sound. Often spelled Lee.
Like 'bahk' with a short, cut-off k, and no r. Often spelled Park.
Like 'chweh' in one beat. Often spelled Choi.

exercises: Split each name into surname (성) and given name (이름): ① 이수진 ② 박서준 ③ 최하나
Write the Korean surname for each English spelling you often see: ① Choi ② Park ③ Lee
Choose the sound that is closer to Korean: ① 이 (ee / lee) ② 박 (bahk / park) ③ 최 (chweh / choy)
Put the parts in Korean order, surname first: ① 지우 + 김 ② 민호 + 최
answers: ① 성: 이, 이름: 수진 ② 성: 박, 이름: 서준 ③ 성: 최, 이름: 하나
① 최 ② 박 ③ 이
① ee ② bahk ③ chweh
